summary: Australian reviewers regard the updated Model 3 as the benchmark electric sedan, praising a supple ride, a well-insulated cabin and strong efficiency, while the touchscreen drive selector and spoke-mounted indicator buttons continue to split opinion. The MY2027 line-up adds a de-contented RWD from $45,900 before on-road costs with 572km of WLTP range, more than the $54,900 Premium RWD's 520km, while the Premium Long Range RWD's 750km WLTP claim remains the longest-range EV sold here. The Performance's $80,900 list price sits above the $75,000 cap that limits the FBT exemption from April 2027, so novated-lease buyers are steered to the three rear-drive grades.
pros: Premium Long Range RWD claims 750km WLTP, the longest range of any EV on sale in Australia, for $61,900 before on-road costs
New base RWD at $45,900 undercuts the BYD Seal Premium ($52,990) and Kia EV4 Air while offering 572km WLTP range and vehicle-to-load
CarExpert measured 12.98kWh/100km in the RWD, well below the 15.3kWh/100km it saw in a Model Y RWD under similar conditions
Access to Tesla's Australian Supercharger network plus regular over-the-air software updates
Supple, comfortable ride and good road and wind noise insulation since the Highland update
cons: Spoke-mounted indicator buttons are easy to press by accident and the touchscreen drive selector slows parking and three-point turns
Base RWD drops the rear passenger touchscreen and ambient lighting and uses part-textile seats to hit its price
Performance's $80,900 list price sits above the $75,000 FBT full-exemption cap that applies from 1 April 2027
Rear headroom and legroom are tighter than in the Model Y, and the five-year warranty trails Kia, MG and BYD
